author: Liu Zhen
description:
China has been urged to learn from a Pentagon project to assess future warfare but warned to avoid the potential conflicts of interest and other shortcomings of the US defence review.
Project Meridian, launched late last month, is designed to identify future battlefield requirements and prioritise investment, with a focus on areas such as artificial intelligence, autonomous systems, directed energy, robotics and biotechnology.
In an analysis published on Friday, the Beijing-based think tank Blue...
title: China urged to copy Pentagon’s hi-tech warfare project without US conflicts of interest

author: Amber Wang
description:
Katie Zacharia may have lasted just five days as the White House press secretary but still managed to set off a diplomatic incident with China.
In an interview with a conservative commentator on Thursday, Zacharia referred to China as a place that “doesn’t even have proper toilets”.
Chinese foreign ministry spokeswoman Mao Ning responded a day later with a smile and a brief, pointed invitation.
“We welcome her to visit China more often when she has the opportunity,” said Mao, a veteran...
title: Katie Zacharia and Mao Ning – a study in contrasts in US and China media strategies

author: Jevans Nyabiage
description:
By the time the Chinese navy hospital ship had docked in the Guinean capital Conakry earlier this month, patients were already queuing for free consultations.
The queues in front of the Auspicious Ark were so long that some people were told to come back the next day, according to Guinean media reports.
The ship, operated by the PLA Navy, offers a range of medical services wherever it stops, including surgery to treat cataracts, appendicitis and hernias as well as gynaecological care. On this...
title: How a hospital ship helps buoy China’s strategic mission in Africa

author: Ling Xin
description:
Professor Qian Jiang, a senior eye expert at Johns Hopkins University in the United States, has moved back to China full time to pursue research on eye transplants.
For more than two decades, Qian built and ran the genetic data hub at Johns Hopkins’ renowned Wilmer Eye Institute. He was welcomed at a ceremony on October 5 at Sir Run Run Shaw Hospital in Hangzhou, part of Zhejiang University, the hospital said.
At the ceremony, Qian said he would also work on “virtual cells” – computer models...
title: Qian Jiang, former Johns Hopkins’ eye institute expert, joins hospital in China

author: Carol Yang
description:
China has condemned Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi for sending a ritual offering to Tokyo’s war-linked Yasukuni Shrine, a move that threatens to further strain ties between the neighbours.
At the start of Yasukuni’s three-day autumn festival on Saturday, Takaichi sent a ritual tree-stand offering to the shrine in her capacity as prime minister, although she did not visit in person.
Minoru Kiuchi, minister in charge of economic growth strategy, visited the controversial site the same day,...
title: China slams Japan’s Takaichi over Yasukuni ritual offering, warns of ‘remilitarisation’

author: Dewey Sim
description:
Chinese Premier Li Qiang has called for deeper cooperation with Uzbekistan in areas such as minerals and artificial intelligence as the Beijing vies with Washington for influence in Central Asia.
Li told President Shavkat Mirziyoyev on Saturday that Beijing was ready to strengthen strategic communication and expand mutually beneficial cooperation with Uzbekistan.
He urged the two countries to step up cooperation in energy, minerals, finance and connectivity, and deepen collaboration in fields...
title: China moves to cement ties with Uzbekistan amid tussle with US for Central Asian influence

author: Eve Qiao
description:
As China marks the 90th anniversary of the Red Army’s victory in the Long March, some young Chinese are looking to the historic journey for guidance as they face uncertainty in their lives and future.
For Lyu Leiyiyi, a 22-year-old student at the Communication University of China, the spirit of the Long March offers a sense of stability at a time when people and the environment around her are changing at a dizzying pace.
“People in their 20s are going through a period of uncertainty,” Lyu said....
title: China’s youth draw upon Long March spirit to navigate modern uncertainties

author: Michael Han
description:
For iPhone users in China, the calendar has long presented a small but recurring problem. On a Sunday designated as a make-up workday, an alarm might remain silent. On a regular Friday converted into a day off, it might ring anyway.
Nearly 17 years after entering the Chinese market, Apple quietly updated its operating system in September to automatically recognise China’s official schedule of adjusted holidays and workdays. The fix is modest, but it points to a larger question: what happens when...
title: China’s ‘golden week’ holidays come at a cost

author: Seong Hyeon Choi
description:
Senior US commanders have highlighted the importance of land-based troops and equipment stationed in the Asia-Pacific in any conflict with China, countering assumptions that such a war would be fought mainly at sea and in the air.
General Ron Clark, commander of US Army Pacific, said the “tyranny of distance” made it difficult to rely on air and naval forces during a panel discussion at the Association of the United States Army’s annual meeting this week.
The comments reflect mounting concerns...
title: How land power could help US forces counter China in the Indo-Pacific
